name: gardner in rounds resting
description: Martin Gardner's minichess (chess on a 5x5 board, each side a rook, knight, bishop, queen and king behind five pawns) played in rounds: each player picks a move in secret, both moves are made together, and a king is simply taken, with no check. One rule shapes the play: the piece that made a side's move rests through that side's next move, unless it is the only piece that can move. A king cannot run two rounds in a row and no piece can strike twice running, so every attack gives a round's warning, and most decided games are won by striking a king that has just moved and so has to stand. Moving at once also blunts the counter-attack: two pieces that try to take each other in the same round simply trade places unharmed (a pawn's diagonal capture just misses), so striking back saves a piece but takes nothing. If both kings fall in the same round, the game is drawn.

provenance.preview: A preview: a new kind of game in which both players move at once, still being tested. Play it against the computer for practice; it is on no leaderboard yet, and its score is a first reading, not yet trusted.
